description: The Fire Rabbit in Chinese astrology: personality, Fire element traits, 1927 and 1987 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Fire Rabbit is the Rabbit born in a Fire year, one of five versions of the fourth animal. It combines the Rabbit's gentleness with Fire's qualities. Fire Rabbit years between 1924 and 2044 are 1927 and 1987. The Rabbit's fixed element is Wood.

sections.heading: The Fire Rabbit personality
paragraphs: Put a Fire stem on the Rabbit and the quiet diplomat finds its voice. The Rabbit's fixed element is Wood, and Wood generates Fire, so this animal is said to kindle the year element from its own resources, turning tact into charm and refinement into flair. Fire Rabbits are frequently portrayed as expressive, affectionate and more openly ambitious than their Wood, Earth or Water cousins. They enjoy company, conversation and a little drama, and they can be persuasive in a warm, disarming way. Because the energy flows out of the Rabbit into Fire, their famously sensitive nerves may fray faster than they expect. Moods can swing between bright sociability and a sudden need to withdraw and recover.

Fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets. Descriptions link it with passion, charisma, courage and a love of movement and expression. Fire-year people are often portrayed as lively, persuasive and quick to act, able to warm a room and rally others behind an idea. The element is associated with the heart and with joy, which gives it real generosity of spirit. Its traditional shadow is impatience: Fire can burn hot and fast, leading to restlessness, sharp words in the moment and a tendency to lose interest once the excitement fades.

sections.heading: Fire Rabbit at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Fire is usually linked with initiative, persuasion and visible leadership. Fire-year people are often described as the ones who launch things, pitch ideas and keep morale high when a deadline looms, which suits performance, sales, media, entrepreneurship and campaigning of every kind. They tend to thrive on momentum and recognition. The traditional caution concerns stamina and follow-through: a Fire stem may lose patience with routine detail, so pairing with methodical colleagues and pacing energy across a project usually helps.

The Fire Rabbit adds sparkle and persuasion to a sign known chiefly for grace. Public relations, hospitality, fashion, theatre and client-facing work are typical matches, since charm is half the job. It flourishes with visible appreciation and a pleasant, well-run workplace, while harsh criticism can wound it more deeply than it lets on. Romantically, the Fire Rabbit is warm and expressive, quick to celebrate a partner's wins with a toast or a handwritten card. Emotional reciprocity and plenty of shared fun matter greatly to it. The awkward pattern is mood: a bruised feeling can flare into a sharp remark, after which the Rabbit side retreats from confrontation and leaves the real issue only half aired.

sections.heading: Fire Rabbit years and dates
paragraphs: Fire Rabbit years in the Lunar New Year table run from February 2, 1927 to January 22, 1928 and from January 29, 1987 to February 16, 1988. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1927 anyone born before Feb 2 is a Fire Tiger, not a Fire Rabbit. Sixty years separate each Fire Rabbit year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Fire Rabbit year is Yin, matching the Rabbit's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Ding-Mao: Ding is the yin Fire stem and Mao is the Rabbit's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Fire Tiger year (before February 2, 1927) and the Fire Tiger year (before January 29, 1987), and births in the weeks after each Fire Rabbit year ends belong to the Earth Dragon. The new year itself fell on a Wednesday in 1927 and Thursday in 1987.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Fire Rabbit
paragraphs: Fire Rabbits tend to thrive when they treat their energy as a budget rather than a bottomless well. Alternating busy social weeks with quieter ones, and protecting sleep, usually keeps their spirits even. Because they feel slights keenly and can respond with a flash of temper, a short pause before replying to a hurtful message is worth cultivating. Creative performance of any kind, from amateur theatre to hosting supper for friends, gives their expressive side a healthy stage. It also helps to have one or two confidants with whom they need not perform at all. Balanced in this way, Fire Rabbits bring real warmth to every circle.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Fire Rabbit shares the Rabbit's San He trine with the Goat and Pig (the Wood trine), its Liu He bond with the Dog, and its Liu Chong clash with the Rooster. The element adds a second layer: another Fire sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Fire in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Fire Rabbit years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1927 (from February 2, 1927) and 1987 (from January 29, 1987). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Fire Rabbit's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Fire and the Rabbit's fixed element is Wood; in the five-element cycles wood generates Fire. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Fire Rabbit?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Goat and Pig (San He) and the Dog (Liu He). The Rooster is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Fire Rabbit called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Ding-Mao. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Fire stem Ding, followed by its earthly branch, here Mao for the Rabbit, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Fire Rabbit different from other Rabbits?
faq.answer: All Rabbits share gentleness, tact and refined taste. The Fire year element changes the tone: fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets.
